6377.stem:
Two teams of athletes were compared on their endurance, as measured by the number of repetitions that they could complete of a short, mixed-activity training circuit. The results are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf-plot below.

\exfigure{308_q17_1}

figures.cap: back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, Team A and Team B

parts.latex: What was the difference between the two teams in terms of the median number of repetitions?
Given that Team B has an interquartile range of 16, show that Team A has a larger interquartile range, and explain what this means in terms of statistical comparison.

solutions.latex:
Reading the plot, Team A has 13 scores:
$$5, 6, 8, 14, 17, 17, 18, 20, 22, 27, 31, 33, 40$$
The median is the 7th score, $18$.

Team B has 12 scores:
$$2, 6, 13, 17, 19, 22, 24, 25, 28, 34, 36, 37$$
The median is the mean of the 6th and 7th scores:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{22 + 24}{2} &= 23 \end{aligned}$$
Difference in medians:
$$\begin{aligned} 23 - 18 &= 5 \end{aligned}$$
The medians differ by $5$ repetitions (Team B higher).

meta.self_check: Re-read stem-and-leaf: A n=13 median 18; B n=12 median 23.

solutions.latex:
For Team A (13 scores), the median is the 7th score. The lower half is the first six scores $5, 6, 8, 14, 17, 17$, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &= \dfrac{8 + 14}{2} \\ &= 11 \end{aligned}$$
The upper half is the last six scores $20, 22, 27, 31, 33, 40$, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 &= \dfrac{27 + 31}{2} \\ &= 29 \end{aligned}$$
Interquartile range of Team A:
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 29 - 11 \\ &= 18 \end{aligned}$$
Since $18 > 16$, Team A has the larger interquartile range.

This means the middle $50\%$ of Team A's results are more spread out, so Team A is less consistent than Team B.
criteria: Finds $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ for Team A, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Team B IQR computed independently as 31-15=16, matching the given value.

308_q17_1.notes: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot drawn in TikZ as a plot, not a grid table (12 Nov ruling). It has the Team A and Team B headings, one rule under the headings, and two vertical rules either side of the stem column. The leaf columns and rows are at the crop's positions with identical values. Lines are 0.6pt where the scan's look heavier (rule 3). Rules: 3, 6b.

6778.stem:
The monthly maximum temperature for Sydney and Melbourne are drawn in the boxplots below.

\exfigure{828_q19_1}

parts.latex: What is the median maximum temperature for Sydney?
Calculate the interquartile range for Melbourne.
Which city has more consistent maximum temperatures? Justify your answer by comparing one measure of spread.

solutions.latex:
From the Sydney box plot, the median is
$$24^\circ\text{C}$$

The interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$ for Melbourne.
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 25 - 16 \\ &= 9^\circ\text{C} \end{aligned}$$

Comparing the interquartile ranges:
$$\text{Sydney } IQR = 5^\circ\text{C} < \text{Melbourne } IQR = 9^\circ\text{C}$$
Or, comparing the ranges:
$$\text{Sydney range} = 9^\circ\text{C} < \text{Melbourne range} = 13^\circ\text{C}$$
Therefore Sydney has more consistent temperatures.

828_q19_1.notes: Two box plots at 0.9pt with grey fill (rule 9): Sydney 17/20/24/25/26 and Melbourne 14/16/21/25/27, on a 12 to 30 scale with light vertical gridlines. Left out the scan's very faint horizontal lines. Title at \footnotesize to match the crop. Overlay 0.88/0.874.
